findings.reason: the plan should have the kernel read `EfitLabels` (declaring the axis/boundary keys on it) and delete the parallel contract, which removes a layer rather than adding one.
findings.text: §6 says the equilibrium kernel (`_integrated_current`, `_axis_and_boundary`) will read a "record contract with canonical keys for the grid, psi, axis and boundary" that the DIII-D loader maps onto, but `imas_ambix/challenge/loader.py:54 EfitLabels` already carries exactly that data (`grid_r_m`, `grid_z_m`, `psirz`, `scalars`, `cocos`) and `ChallengeShot` already wraps it; a separate canonical-key contract is a second representation of one record and gives the DIII-D path two shapes for the same equilibrium

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new modules hide substantial behaviour behind small interfaces: `selene_deck.py` is one converter entry point over three deck grammars plus IDS emission and receipts; `tokamap_export.py` exposes one public function (`export_tokamap_directory`, imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py:349) over key mapping, unit/sign/COCOS collapse and group filtering; `eddb.py` exposes `fetch_channels`/`write_channel`/`is_cached`/`channel_path` over transport-free cache state. No section spreads one behaviour across shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 proposes a new canonical-key equilibrium record contract (grid, psi, axis, boundary) that duplicates the typed record `challenge/loader.py` already owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. Every section that adds surface states in its own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be: §2 "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §3 "retire nothing ... merge into nothing, because the FAIR-MAST mirror ... downloads from an object store"; §4 "widens one protocol method and retires nothing"; §7 "adds two record fields and retires nothing". No section adds to any of the four families without that accounting.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the mechanism it extends for every layer it touches, and each named mechanism exists: `load_packaged_signal_map` (imas_ambix/data/signal_map.py:631), `read_geometry_table` and `_supply_declared_probe_angles` (imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py:113,53), the identity proofs (imas_ambix/data/description_identity.py:67,106,129), the convention owners (imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py:329 score_convention, :606 format_sign_report; imas_ambix/challenge/convention.py:266 measure_diiid_convention), the gated reference seam (imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py:120 read_efit_geometry, :272 judge_geometry), the artifact resolver (imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py:304,344), the remote store (imas_ambix/data/eddb.py:208 write_channel, imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py:160 SshTransport), the declaration classes (imas_ambix/data/machine_map.py:767 FluxLoopPositionDeclaration, :1033 flux_loop_positions_for), the shot set (imas_ambix/spine_bench/shots.py:27,60) and the residual owner (imas_ambix/spine_bench/runner.py:161). The plan also correctly reports a genuine absence — no shot→catalogue mapping exists (`grep` for `machine_for_shot` returns nothing) and DIII-D's map spans 0–2147483647 (imas_ambix/data/machine_maps/diii-d.json), so `map_for_shot` cannot disambiguate — which is why the machine must be declared rather than inferred.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every proposed layer states why the owner is extended rather than a parallel path built: §4 widens `StoreEngine.open` for the selected map rather than adding an engine; §6 generalises `measure_diiid_convention` rather than writing a second scorer; §7 reuses `SshTransport` rather than a second remote path and adds a grid writer beside `write_channel` in the same store.
